subproblem.title: Local-to-global gluing of co-area identities through an injective continuous chart (Lindelöf, disjointification, countable additivity)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P continuous on all of ℝⁿ and injective on Ω, W ⊆ Φ(Ω) Borel, f : ℝ^P → ℝ Borel, J, g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] arbitrary and μ, ν measures on ℝ^P. Suppose every w₀ ∈ Ω with Φ(w₀) ∈ W has an open neighbourhood O such that for every Borel S ⊆ O ∩ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(W), t ↦ ∫_{Φ(S) ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dν is Lebesgue-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{Φ(S) ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dν dt = ∫_{Φ(S)} J g dμ. Then t ↦ ∫_{W ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dν is Lebesgue-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{W ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dν dt = ∫_W J g dμ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (W : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (J g : Eucl P → ℝ≥0∞) (μ ν : Measure (Eucl P)), IsOpen Ω → Continuous Φ → InjOn Φ Ω → Measurable f → MeasurableSet W → W ⊆ Φ '' Ω → (∀ w₀ ∈ Ω, Φ w₀ ∈ W → ∃ O : Set (Eucl n), IsOpen O ∧ w₀ ∈ O ∧ ∀ S : Set (Eucl n), MeasurableSet S → S ⊆ O ∩ (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' W) → AEMeasurable (fun t : ℝ => ∫⁻ x in Φ '' S ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂ν) (volume : Measure ℝ) ∧ ∫⁻ t, (∫⁻ x in Φ '' S ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂ν) ∂(volume : Measure ℝ) = ∫⁻ x in Φ '' S, J x * g x ∂μ) → AEMeasurable (fun t : ℝ => ∫⁻ x in W ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂ν) (volume : Measure ℝ) ∧ ∫⁻ t, (∫⁻ x in W ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂ν) ∂(volume : Measure ℝ) = ∫⁻ x in W, J x * g x ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
This is step 6 of the parent proof (cover and glue). The remainder W ∖ ⋃_k W_k is empty, so the gluing is done directly by countable additivity, which is the argument of the gluing lemma with empty remainder.

Notation: for a Borel S ⊆ ℝⁿ, (LP)(S) is the statement "t ↦ ∫_{Φ(S) ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dν is Lebesgue-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{Φ(S) ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dν dt = ∫_{Φ(S)} J g dμ". Integrals over a set are integrals against the restricted measure.

1. (The set E.) E := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(W) is Borel (Ω open, Φ continuous, W Borel). Φ(E) = W: ⊆ is clear, and each x ∈ W is Φ(w) with w ∈ Ω because W ⊆ Φ(Ω), so w ∈ E.
2. (Local sets for all points.) (LP)(∅) holds: every set integral over ∅ vanishes, so the slice function is the constant 0 (measurable) and both sides are 0. For w ∈ E, the hypothesis gives an open O(w) ∋ w with (LP)(S) for all Borel S ⊆ O(w) ∩ E. For w ∉ E put O(w) := ∅; then every S ⊆ O(w) ∩ E is ∅ and (LP)(S) holds. So every w ∈ ℝⁿ has an open O(w) with (w ∈ E ⇒ w ∈ O(w)) and (LP)(S) for all Borel S ⊆ O(w) ∩ E (choose).
3. (Lindelöf.) ℝⁿ is second countable, so TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable gives a countable T with ⋃_{w∈T} O(w) = ⋃_w O(w) ⊇ E. Choose e : ℕ → ℝⁿ with T ⊆ range e (Set.countable_iff_exists_subset_range). Put A_k := E ∩ O(e_k). These are Borel and ⋃_k A_k = E: if w ∈ E, then w ∈ O(w) ⊆ ⋃_{u∈T} O(u), so w ∈ O(e_k) for some k.
4. (Disjointification.) D_k := disjointed A k = A_k ∖ ⋃_{l<k} A_l. The D_k are Borel (MeasurableSet.disjointed), pairwise disjoint (disjoint_disjointed), and ⋃_k D_k = ⋃_k A_k = E (iUnion_disjointed). Also D_k ⊆ A_k ⊆ O(e_k) ∩ E, so (LP)(D_k) holds for every k by step 2.
5. (Images.) W_k := Φ(D_k) is Borel by Lusin–Souslin (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn: D_k is Borel in the Polish space ℝⁿ, and Φ is continuous and injective on D_k ⊆ Ω). The W_k are pairwise disjoint: for i ≠ j, Φ(D_i) ∩ Φ(D_j) = Φ(D_i ∩ D_j) = ∅ by injectivity on Ω (InjOn.image_inter). ⋃_k W_k = Φ(⋃_k D_k) = Φ(E) = W.
6. (Slices.) For each t ∈ ℝ, W ∩ f⁻¹{t} = ⋃_k (W_k ∩ f⁻¹{t}). These sets are Borel (f measurable) and pairwise disjoint, so countable additivity of the set integral (lintegral_iUnion; no measurability of g is needed) gives ∫_{W ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dν = Σ_k ∫_{W_k ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dν.
7. (Measurability.) By (LP)(D_k), each t ↦ ∫_{W_k ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dν is a.e.-measurable, so their sum, which by step 6 is the slice function of W, is a.e.-measurable (AEMeasurable.tsum). This is the first conjunct.
8. (Identity.) ∫_ℝ ∫_{W ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dν dt = ∫_ℝ Σ_k ∫_{W_k ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dν dt = Σ_k ∫_ℝ ∫_{W_k ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dν dt (lintegral_tsum, valid for a.e.-measurable summands) = Σ_k ∫_{W_k} J g dμ (by (LP)(D_k)) = ∫_W J g dμ (lintegral_iUnion for the disjoint Borel W_k with ⋃_k W_k = W). This is the second conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: E := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹W is Borel and Φ(E) = W.
Choose open O(w) for every w (∅ off E); Lindelöf gives countably many O(e_k) covering E.
Disjointify A_k := E ∩ O(e_k) into Borel D_k with ⋃D_k = E and the local property for each D_k.
W_k := Φ(D_k) are Borel (Lusin–Souslin), pairwise disjoint (injectivity) and cover W.
Countable additivity (lintegral_iUnion) for the slices and for W; AEMeasurable.tsum and lintegral_tsum give both conjuncts.

subproblem.title: Jacobian identity for the slice map: J_m(A∘D∘ι) = |γ|·J_n(A)·|det D| in Gram-determinant form
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m+1, A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and D : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ continuous linear maps, and γ ∈ ℝ^P with γ ∈ range A and ⟨γ, A(D y)⟩ = y_0 for every y ∈ ℝⁿ. With e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1, √det(⟨A D e_{i+1}, A D e_{j+1}⟩)_{i,j<m} = |γ| · √det(⟨A e_i, A e_j⟩)_{i,j<n} · |det D|. No injectivity of A or invertibility of D is assumed; for m = 0 the left side is √(det of the empty matrix) = 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (A : Eucl (m + 1) →L[ℝ] Eucl P) (D : Eucl (m + 1) →L[ℝ] Eucl (m + 1)) (γ : Eucl P), γ ∈ LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap → (∀ y : Eucl (m + 1), inner ℝ γ (A (D y)) = y 0) → Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin m => inner ℝ (A (D (EuclideanSpace.single i.succ 1))) (A (D (EuclideanSpace.single j.succ 1)))).det = ‖γ‖ * Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin (m + 1) => inner ℝ (A (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (A (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det * |D.det|
subproblem.natural_proof:
This is step 4 of the parent proof (the Jacobian identity J_m(A∘D∘ι) = |ĝ|·J_n(A)·|det D|, ι(z) := [0,z]), in Gram-determinant form and without the injectivity of A or the invertibility of D: in degenerate cases both sides vanish. In the parent's application A = DΦ(w), D = Dχ(y), γ = G(Φ(w)), and the left side is J_m of the slice map. We use a Gram-matrix/Cramer computation instead of the block-triangular normDet computation; it proves the same identity and needs no orthonormal bases of subspaces.

Notation. n := m+1, e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i < n). v_j := A(D e_j) for j < n. Γ := (⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j<n} (an n×n real matrix); Γ′ := Γ.submatrix Fin.succ Fin.succ = (⟨v_{i+1}, v_{j+1}⟩)_{i,j<m}, which is exactly the matrix on the left-hand side; G_A := (⟨A e_i, A e_j⟩)_{i,j<n}; [D] is the matrix of D in the standard basis, [D]_{k i} := (D e_i)_k (LinearMap.toMatrix for EuclideanSpace.basisFun), so det [D] = D.det (LinearMap.det_toMatrix).

1. (Dual relation.) For j < n the hypothesis with y := e_j gives ⟨γ, v_j⟩ = (e_j)_0, which is 1 if j = 0 and 0 otherwise.
2. (Γ = [D]ᵀ G_A [D].) Expanding in the standard basis, D e_i = Σ_k [D]_{k i} e_k, so by linearity v_i = Σ_k [D]_{k i} A e_k. Bilinearity of the inner product gives ⟨v_i, v_j⟩ = Σ_k Σ_l [D]_{k i} ⟨A e_k, A e_l⟩ [D]_{l j} = ([D]ᵀ G_A [D])_{i j}. Hence det Γ = det([D])² · det G_A = (D.det)² · det G_A (Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_transpose).
3. (Claim: det Γ′ = |γ|² · det Γ.)
(a) Case D.det = 0. Then D is not injective (LinearMap.bot_lt_ker_of_det_eq_zero); pick y ≠ 0 with D y = 0. The hypothesis gives y_0 = ⟨γ, A(D y)⟩ = 0. Put z := (y_1, …, y_m) ∈ ℝ^m (z i := y (i.succ)); z ≠ 0 because y ≠ 0 and y_0 = 0. (For m = 0 this case cannot occur: the hypothesis with y = e_0 gives ⟨γ, A(D e_0)⟩ = 1, so D ≠ 0 and, D being 1×1, D.det ≠ 0.) Since y_0 = 0, y = Σ_{j<m} z_j e_{j+1}, so Σ_j z_j v_{j+1} = A(D y) = 0, and (Γ′ z)_i = ⟨v_{i+1}, Σ_j z_j v_{j+1}⟩ = 0 for every i. So Γ′ has a nonzero kernel vector and det Γ′ = 0 (Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff). By step 2, det Γ = 0, and the claim reads 0 = 0.
(b) Case D.det ≠ 0. Then D is bijective (ContinuousLinearMap.toContinuousLinearEquivOfDetNeZero). As γ ∈ range A, γ = A u₀ for some u₀; let c := D⁻¹ u₀, so γ = A(D c) = Σ_j c_j v_j (expand c = Σ_j c_j e_j). For every i, (Γ c)_i = Σ_j ⟨v_i, v_j⟩ c_j = ⟨v_i, γ⟩ = δ_{i0} by step 1, i.e. Γ *ᵥ c = Pi.single 0 1. Moreover |γ|² = ⟨γ, Σ_j c_j v_j⟩ = Σ_j c_j ⟨γ, v_j⟩ = c_0. Cramer's rule: cramer Γ b = adjugate Γ *ᵥ b and adjugate Γ * Γ = det Γ • 1, so cramer Γ (Γ *ᵥ c) = det Γ • c; evaluating at 0 (Matrix.cramer_apply), det Γ · c_0 = det(Γ.updateCol 0 (Pi.single 0 1)). Expand this determinant along column 0 (Matrix.det_succ_column_zero): column 0 is the vector Pi.single 0 1, so only the row-0 term survives, with sign +1 and minor obtained by deleting row 0 and column 0; that minor is Γ′, because the other columns are those of Γ. Hence det Γ′ = det Γ · c_0 = |γ|² · det Γ.
4. (Combine.) By steps 2 and 3, det Γ′ = |γ|² · (D.det)² · det G_A.
5. (Square roots.) √(det Γ′) = √(|γ|² · (D.det)²) · √(det G_A) (Real.sqrt_mul, the first factor is ≥ 0) = |γ| · |D.det| · √(det G_A) (Real.sqrt_sq for |γ| ≥ 0, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs), which is the asserted identity after reordering the factors. No sign condition on det G_A is needed. For m = 0, Γ′ is the empty matrix with determinant 1, and all steps remain valid. ∎
proof_key_steps: Dual relation ⟨γ, A D e_j⟩ = δ_{j0} from the hypothesis.
Gram matrix Γ of v_j = A D e_j equals [D]ᵀ G_A [D], so det Γ = (det D)² det G_A.
If det D = 0: a kernel vector y of D has y_0 = 0, so its tail is a nonzero kernel vector of Γ′ and det Γ′ = 0 = RHS.
If det D ≠ 0: γ = Σ c_j v_j with Γc = e_0 and |γ|² = c_0; Cramer's rule and Laplace expansion along column 0 give det Γ′ = c_0 det Γ.
det Γ′ = |γ|² (det D)² det G_A; take square roots (Real.sqrt_mul, sqrt_sq_eq_abs).

Square-root factorization is valid, including m = 0. Matrix.of ensures the intended matrix constructions.

Notation: n := m+1, [t,v] := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)).

1. (Coordinate map.) J : ℝ × ℝ^m → ℝⁿ, J(a,b) := [a,b], is continuous linear (check additivity and homogeneity coordinatewise with Fin.cases), injective (Fin.cons_inj, injectivity of EuclideanSpace.equiv), and J(a,b)_0 = a.
2. (Projection π.) ℓ := Dh(w₀) ≠ 0 is a nonzero linear functional on ℝⁿ, so K := ker ℓ has dimension m (Module.Dual.finrank_ker_add_one_of_ne_zero and finrank ℝⁿ = m+1). Put π := ι_K ∘ P_K : ℝⁿ → ℝ^m (continuous linear). Then |π u| = |P_K u| ≤ |u| for all u (Submodule.norm_orthogonalProjectionOnto_apply_le), and if ℓ u = 0 and π u = 0, then u ∈ K, so P_K u = u and ι_K u = 0, hence u = 0. DΨ(w₀) is injective: if DΨ(w₀)u₁ = DΨ(w₀)u₂, injectivity of J gives ℓ(u₁ − u₂) = 0 and π(u₁ − u₂) = 0, so u₁ = u₂ by step 2. An injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional ℝⁿ is bijective; let e₀ : ℝⁿ ≃L[ℝ] ℝⁿ be the equivalence with (e₀ : ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ) = DΨ(w₀) (LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo, toContinuousLinearEquiv).

9. (Slice antilipschitz bound.) If [t,v] ∈ B, step 8 gives J(h(χ[t,v]), π(χ[t,v])) = [t,v] = J(t, v), so π(χ[t,v]) = v by injectivity of J. For [t,v], [t,v′] ∈ B, linearity of π and |π u| ≤ |u| give |v − v′| = |π(χ[t,v]) − π(χ[t,v′])| = |π(χ[t,v] − χ[t,v′])| ≤ |χ[t,v] − χ[t,v′]|.
Steps 6–9 give all conjuncts. The case m = 0 needs no change: K = 0 and ℝ^0 is a point. ∎

subproblem.title: Tonelli in the coordinates ℝ^{m+1} = ℝ × ℝ^m
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ and F : ℝ^{m+1} → [0, ∞] be Borel. For t ∈ ℝ and v ∈ ℝ^m let [t,v] ∈ ℝ^{m+1} be the point (t, v_0, …, v_{m−1}), i.e. (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)). Then t ↦ ∫_{ℝ^m} F([t,v]) dL^m(v) is Borel measurable and ∫_{ℝ^{m+1}} F dL^{m+1} = ∫_ℝ ∫_{ℝ^m} F([t,v]) dL^m(v) dt (Lebesgue measures = volume).

Notation: for t ∈ ℝ and v ∈ ℝ^m, [t,v] := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)) and e(t,v) := [t,v], e : ℝ × ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+1}. All measures are volume (Lebesgue measure); volume on Fin k → ℝ is Measure.pi (fun _ => volume) (volume_pi).

1. (e is measure preserving from volume.prod volume to volume.) e is the composite of three measure-preserving maps:
(a) (t, v) ↦ (t, WithLp.ofLp v), ℝ × ℝ^m → ℝ × (Fin m → ℝ): MeasurePreserving.prod of MeasurePreserving.id and PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp (Fin m) (= EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp);
(b) (t, x) ↦ Fin.cons t x, ℝ × (Fin m → ℝ) → (Fin (m+1) → ℝ): this is (MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) 0).symm, since Fin.insertNth 0 = Fin.cons (MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove_symm_apply, Fin.insertNthEquiv_zero), and it is measure preserving by (MeasureTheory.measurePreserving_piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => volume) 0).symm (equivalently volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove);
(c) WithLp.toLp : (Fin (m+1) → ℝ) → ℝ^{m+1}: PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp (Fin (m+1)).
EuclideanSpace.equiv is ofLp and its inverse is toLp, so the composite (c)∘(b)∘(a) is e, by funext and simp. Hence MeasurePreserving e (volume.prod volume) volume.
2. F ∘ e is measurable (F measurable, e measurable). By MeasurePreserving.lintegral_comp, ∫ F dL^{m+1} = ∫ (F ∘ e) d(L¹ ⊗ L^m).
3. Tonelli (lintegral_prod with (F ∘ e).aemeasurable; volume on ℝ^m is σ-finite): ∫ (F ∘ e) d(L¹ ⊗ L^m) = ∫_ℝ ∫_{ℝ^m} F([t,v]) dv dt. With step 2 this is the second conjunct.
4. Measurability (Measurable.lintegral_prod_right' applied to the measurable F ∘ e on ℝ × ℝ^m): t ↦ ∫_{ℝ^m} F([t,v]) dv is measurable. This is the first conjunct. ∎

subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m+1, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P of class C¹, K-Lipschitz on Ω and c-antilipschitz on Ω (c > 0), h : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C¹, f : ℝ^P → ℝ arbitrary, G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Borel, B ⊆ ℝⁿ open and χ : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ of class C¹ on B with χ(B) ⊆ Ω, χ Lipschitz on B, h(χ(y)) = y_0 for y ∈ B, and |v − v′| ≤ |χ([t,v]) − χ([t,v′])| whenever [t,v], [t,v′] ∈ B ([t,v] = (t, v_0, …, v_{m−1})). Let S ⊆ χ(B) be Borel with f(Φ(w)) = h(w), G(Φ(w)) ∈ range DΦ(w) and ⟨G(Φ(w)), DΦ(w)u⟩ = Dh(w)u (all u) for every w ∈ S. Then for every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], t ↦ ∫_{Φ(S) ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m is Lebesgue-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{Φ(S) ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m dt = ∫_{Φ(S)} |G| g dH^{m+1} (Hᵏ := μHE[k]).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl (m + 1) → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (h : Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (G : Eucl P → Eucl P) (B : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (χ : Eucl (m + 1) → Eucl (m + 1)) (S : Set (Eucl (m + 1))), IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith K Φ Ω) → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → ContDiff ℝ 1 h → Measurable G → IsOpen B → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 χ B → χ '' B ⊆ Ω → (∃ Λ : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith Λ χ B) → (∀ y ∈ B, h (χ y) = y 0) → (∀ (t : ℝ) (v v' : Eucl m), (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)) ∈ B → (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v')) ∈ B → ‖v - v'‖ ≤ ‖χ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v))) - χ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v')))‖) → MeasurableSet S → S ⊆ χ '' B → (∀ w ∈ S, f (Φ w) = h w ∧ G (Φ w) ∈ LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w).toLinearMap ∧ ∀ u, inner ℝ (G (Φ w)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w u) = fderiv ℝ h w u) → ∀ g : Eucl P → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g → AEMeasurable (fun t : ℝ => ∫⁻ x in Φ '' S ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂(μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P))) (volume : Measure ℝ) ∧ ∫⁻ t, (∫⁻ x in Φ '' S ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂(μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P))) ∂(volume : Measure ℝ) = ∫⁻ x in Φ '' S, ‖G x‖ₑ * g x ∂(μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. n := m+1. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Lᵏ = volume on ℝᵏ; Hᵏ := μHE[k] on ℝ^P. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. For t ∈ ℝ and v ∈ ℝ^m, [t,v] := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)) is the point (t, v_0, …, v_{m−1}) of ℝ^{m+1}; for y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, tail y := (y_1, …, y_m) ∈ ℝ^m, so that y = [y_0, tail y]. D := fderiv ℝ. For F : ℝᵏ → ℝ^Q and x ∈ ℝᵏ, J_kF(x) := √det(⟨DF(x)e_i, DF(x)e_j⟩)_{i,j<k} (Gram-determinant Jacobian; the determinant of the empty matrix is 1).

This is steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 of the parent proof on one straightened box. The chart (B, χ) is now a hypothesis; the parent proof constructs it in step 2. Sibling lemmas used: area_formula (Submission.lpf_raf_chart_change_of_variables), jacobian (Submission.slicing_im_creg_jacobian_identity) and tonelli (Submission.slicing_im_creg_lintegral_cons). Mathlib results used: change of variables MeasureTheory.lintegral_image_eq_lintegral_abs_det_fderiv_mul, and Lusin–Souslin MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn. Fix K, c > 0 and Λ from the hypotheses.

1. (Coordinates.) [t,v]_0 = t and [t,v]_{i+1} = v_i; [y_0, tail y] = y. With ι : ℝ^m → ℝⁿ, ι(z) := [0,z], a linear map with |ι z| = |z|, [t,v] = [t,0] + ι(v). So v ↦ [t,v] is affine with derivative ι, 1-Lipschitz and continuous, |[t,v] − [t,v′]| = |v − v′|, and ι(e_i) = e_{i+1} for i < m.
2. (Injectivity.) Φ is injective on Ω: if w, w′ ∈ Ω and Φ(w) = Φ(w′), then c|w − w′| ≤ 0 with c > 0. χ is injective on B: if y, y′ ∈ B and χ(y) = χ(y′), then y_0 = h(χ y) = h(χ y′) = y′_0 =: t. With v := tail y and v′ := tail y′ we have y = [t,v] and y′ = [t,v′] in B, so the slice hypothesis gives |v − v′| ≤ |χ y − χ y′| = 0, hence y = y′.
3. (Derivatives.) B is open and χ is C¹ on B, so χ has derivative Dχ(y) at each y ∈ B (HasFDerivAt). Φ and h are differentiable. Since h(χ(y′)) = y′_0 for all y′ in the neighbourhood B of y, the chain rule and uniqueness of derivatives give Dh(χ y)(Dχ(y) z) = z_0 for all z (the derivative of y′ ↦ y′_0 is EuclideanSpace.proj 0). For [t,v] ∈ B, the slice map σ_t(v) := Φ(χ([t,v])) has derivative DΦ(χ[t,v]) ∘ Dχ([t,v]) ∘ ι at v. So Dσ_t(v)e_i = DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y) e_{i+1}) with y = [t,v], and J_mσ_t(v) = 𝒥(y), where 𝒥(y) := √det(⟨DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{i+1}), DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{j+1})⟩)_{i,j<m}.
4. (Sets.) Let S′ := B ∩ χ⁻¹(S). It is Borel: χ̃ := B.piecewise χ 0 is Borel measurable (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise; χ is continuous on the open set B), and S′ = B ∩ χ̃⁻¹(S). χ(S′) = S because S ⊆ χ(B). Also S ⊆ χ(B) ⊆ Ω. Φ(S) is Borel by Lusin–Souslin, since Φ is continuous and injective on the Borel set S. Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Φ(S)) = S by injectivity of Φ on Ω.
5. (Area formula for Φ.) Apply area_formula with n := m+1, the chart Φ on the open set Ω (K-Lipschitz and c-antilipschitz), A := Φ(S) ⊆ Φ(Ω) (Borel, so null-measurable) and the Borel weight x ↦ ‖G x‖ₑ·g(x). By step 4, Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Φ(S)) = S, so ∫_{Φ(S)} ‖G‖ₑ g dH^{m+1} = ∫_S F dLⁿ, where F(w) := ‖G(Φ w)‖ₑ · g(Φ w) · ofReal(J_{m+1}Φ(w)).
6. (Change of variables along χ.) Apply lintegral_image_eq_lintegral_abs_det_fderiv_mul (μ := volume on ℝⁿ) to the Borel set S′. Its hypotheses are HasFDerivWithinAt χ (Dχ y) S′ y for y ∈ S′ (step 3) and χ injective on S′ ⊆ B (step 2). Applied to F, and using χ(S′) = S: ∫_S F dLⁿ = ∫_{S′} ofReal|det Dχ(y)| · F(χ y) dLⁿ(y).
7. (Jacobian identity.) Let y ∈ S′ and w := χ(y) ∈ S. By the pointwise hypothesis, γ := G(Φ w) ∈ range DΦ(w) and ⟨γ, DΦ(w)u⟩ = Dh(w)u for all u. With u := Dχ(y)z and step 3, ⟨γ, DΦ(w)(Dχ(y)z)⟩ = z_0 for all z. Apply jacobian with A := DΦ(w) and D := Dχ(y): 𝒥(y) = |G(Φ w)| · J_{m+1}Φ(w) · |det Dχ(y)|. Using ENNReal.ofReal_mul (all factors ≥ 0) and ‖·‖ₑ = ofReal ‖·‖ (ofReal_norm), ofReal|det Dχ(y)| · F(χ y) = g(Φ(χ y)) · ofReal(𝒥(y)) on S′. Hence, by setLIntegral_congr_fun and lintegral_indicator (S′ Borel), ∫_{S′} ofReal|det Dχ| · F∘χ dLⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} F̃ dLⁿ, where F̃ := S′.indicator (y ↦ g(Φ(χ y)) · ofReal(𝒥(y))).
8. (F̃ is Borel.) On S′ ⊆ B, χ = χ̃, so F̃ = S′.indicator (y ↦ g(Φ(χ̃ y)) · ofReal √det M(y)) with M(y)_{ij} := ⟨DΦ(χ̃ y)(Dχ(y)e_{i+1}), DΦ(χ̃ y)(Dχ(y)e_{j+1})⟩. Each piece is measurable: χ̃ (step 4); y ↦ Dχ(y)e_k (measurable_fderiv_apply_const); (x,u) ↦ DΦ(x)u, which is continuous because Φ is C¹ (Continuous.measurable2); inner products (Measurable.inner); the matrix (Measurable.of_eval_matrix); det and √, which are continuous; and g∘Φ∘χ̃. So F̃ is measurable (Measurable.indicator).
9. (Tonelli.) Apply tonelli to F̃: τ(t) := ∫_{ℝ^m} F̃([t,v]) dv is measurable in t, and ∫_{ℝⁿ} F̃ dLⁿ = ∫_ℝ τ(t) dt.
10. (Slices: area formula for σ_t.) Fix t ∈ ℝ. B_t := {v : [t,v] ∈ B} is open (preimage of the open B under the continuous v ↦ [t,v]). S′_t := {v : [t,v] ∈ S′} ⊆ B_t is Borel. On B_t, σ_t is K·Λ-Lipschitz by LipschitzOnWith.comp: v ↦ [t,v] is 1-Lipschitz and maps B_t into B, χ is Λ-Lipschitz on B with χ(B) ⊆ Ω, and Φ is K-Lipschitz on Ω. σ_t is also c-antilipschitz on B_t: c|v − v′| ≤ c|χ[t,v] − χ[t,v′]| ≤ |σ_t v − σ_t v′|, by the slice hypothesis and the antilipschitz bound of Φ on Ω ⊇ χ(B). So σ_t is continuous and injective on B_t; A_t := σ_t(S′_t) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin) and B_t ∩ σ_t⁻¹(A_t) = S′_t. Apply area_formula with n := m, the chart σ_t on the open set B_t, A := A_t ⊆ σ_t(B_t) and the weight g: ∫_{A_t} g dH^m = ∫_{S′_t} g(σ_t v) · ofReal(J_mσ_t(v)) dv. For v ∈ S′_t, J_mσ_t(v) = 𝒥([t,v]) (step 3) and g(σ_t v) = g(Φ(χ[t,v])); for v ∉ S′_t, F̃([t,v]) = 0. Hence ∫_{A_t} g dH^m = ∫_{ℝ^m} F̃([t,v]) dv = τ(t) (lintegral_indicator and lintegral_congr). If B_t = ∅, all terms are 0. For m = 0 this is the counting-measure case of area_formula, with J_0 = 1.
11. (Slice sets.) A_t = Φ(S) ∩ f⁻¹{t}.
(⊇) Let w ∈ S with f(Φ w) = t. Then w = χ(y) with y ∈ B (S ⊆ χ(B)), so y ∈ S′, and y_0 = h(χ y) = h(w) = f(Φ w) = t. Thus y = [t, tail y], tail y ∈ S′_t and σ_t(tail y) = Φ(w).
(⊆) If v ∈ S′_t, then χ[t,v] ∈ S, so σ_t(v) = Φ(χ[t,v]) ∈ Φ(S), and f(σ_t v) = h(χ[t,v]) = [t,v]_0 = t.
12. (Conclusion.) By steps 10–11, ∫_{Φ(S) ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m = τ(t) for every t ∈ ℝ. So the slice function equals the measurable τ and is AEMeasurable (Measurable.aemeasurable, AEMeasurable.congr). Chaining steps 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10–11 gives ∫_{Φ(S)} ‖G‖ₑ g dH^{m+1} = ∫_S F = ∫_{S′} ofReal|det Dχ|·F∘χ = ∫ F̃ = ∫_ℝ τ(t) dt = ∫_ℝ ∫_{Φ(S) ∩ f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m dt. ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ injective on Ω; χ injective on B (h∘χ = y_0 plus the slice bound); S′ := B ∩ χ⁻¹S Borel with χ(S′) = S; Φ(S) Borel (Lusin–Souslin).
Chain rule: Dh(χy)∘Dχ(y) = proj_0 on B; Dσ_t(v)e_i = DΦ(χy)(Dχ(y)e_{i+1}).
Area formula (lpf_raf_chart_change_of_variables) for Φ on Ω turns ∫_{Φ(S)} ‖G‖ₑ g dH^{m+1} into ∫_S ‖G∘Φ‖ₑ g∘Φ JΦ.
Change of variables along χ on S′ (lintegral_image_eq_lintegral_abs_det_fderiv_mul).
Jacobian identity (slicing_im_creg_jacobian_identity) with A = DΦ(χy), D = Dχ(y), γ = G(Φχy) rewrites the integrand as g∘Φ∘χ·𝒥, giving a Borel F̃ on ℝⁿ.
Tonelli (slicing_im_creg_lintegral_cons) splits ∫F̃ into ∫_t τ(t), τ measurable.
For each t, the area formula for the Lipschitz, antilipschitz slice map σ_t on the open B_t gives τ(t) = ∫_{σ_t(S′_t)} g dH^m, and σ_t(S′_t) = Φ(S) ∩ f⁻¹{t}.

audit.reason: The stated hypotheses imply injectivity of χ and Dh∘Dχ = proj₀. Both area-formula applications, change of variables, the Jacobian identity and Tonelli satisfy their hypotheses. The measurable extension handles χ outside B. Slice images are Borel despite arbitrary f. The proof uses exactly the three declared dependencies and proves both conclusions.
